sections.heading: When this job comes up
body: Customer has drain flies. Mitch's service is called Drain Fly Treatment. Past invoices read: "Drain fly treatment", "Drain fly treatment, second treatment" and "External fly treatment only including residual treatment to common fly activity areas around the property".

Drain flies (also called moth flies) breed where it is damp and there is a build-up of organic gunk, like bathroom drains, open drains and septic run-off. So the fix is the breeding spot, not just the flies you can see.
The job process, the never list, PPE and the free service period are in the Every job guide.

sections.heading: What the law and the label require

items.detail: Using a pesticide against its label is an offence. If the job needs something the label does not allow, stop and call Mitch.

items.text: Make the record the same day
items.detail: Every pesticide job needs a record: full product name, date, target pest, rate and quantity, address and area treated, who applied it, equipment, and start and finish times. It must be made within 48 hours and kept at least 3 years. Give the customer a copy if they ask.

items.text: Only do work your licence covers
items.detail: If a treatment is outside your licence class, work under Mitch's direct supervision and do not do it alone.

items.text: Protect people, pets and the environment
items.detail: Wear the PPE the label and SDS call for. Keep spray and bait away from people, pets, food, drains and waterways. Harming people, wildlife or property with a pesticide is an offence.

sections.heading: How to tell it is drain fly
rows: Tiny dark grey flies, 2 to 4 mm
Drain (moth) flies. The body is covered in fine hairs, and the wings are moth-like with a hairy fringe.
Flies around bathrooms, open drains or septic run-off
That is where moth flies are usually found, anywhere it is damp.
Small brown and yellow or brown and black flies, 2.5 to 4 mm, around fruit and veg
Not drain flies. They are vinegar (fruit) flies. They go for ripe or rotting fruit and veg.

items.text: Bathrooms, and any drain or damp spot the customer says the flies are around
items.detail: Locate where the larvae (the grubs) are breeding if you can, and probe for hidden spots.

items.text: Open drains and septic run-off outside

items.detail: Mitch will show you how on the ride-along. Until then, follow the product label.

items.a: Drain flies, also called moth flies. They're tiny, dark grey and hairy, and they look a bit like a little moth. You find them where it's damp, like bathrooms and drains.

items.q: Why do I keep getting them?
items.a: They breed in the damp build-up in and around drains. New flies keep turning up until the breeding spot is dealt with, so that's what we treat.

items.q: Are they the same as fruit flies?
items.a: No. Fruit flies go for ripe or rotting fruit and veg. Drain flies come from damp build-up in drains.
Only in big numbers is there any concern, and that's an allergic reaction in some people if they breathe them in. Sorting out the breeding spot is the fix.

items.q: How do I stop them coming back?
items.a: Keep the damp spots clean so gunk doesn't build up, keep bins closed and dry, and use screens on windows and doors where you can.

items.q: Is it safe for the kids and pets?
items.a: Keep kids and pets out of the area while we treat. Follow the product label for when it's safe to come back in. We normally say 1 to 2 hours once it's dry.
